metatype.value: The prevalence of undernourishment is a widely used measure for monitoring hunger and progress toward ensuring access to sufficient food. It captures the extent of dietary energy inadequacy in a population, reflecting changes in the overall availability of food, households' ability to access it, and the socio-demographic characteristics of the population.

The prevalence of undernourishment is a model-based estimate, and its reliability depends on the quality of the data used to estimate the model parameters. Measurement errors may affect estimates of dietary energy consumption derived from household surveys and Food Balance Sheets. Because of the probabilistic nature of the estimation and uncertainty associated with the model parameters, the precision of PoU estimates is generally low. National-level PoU point estimates are available only when they exceed 2.5 percent. The indicator cannot identify which individuals in a population are undernourished and, in the absence of representative food-consumption data at the subnational level, can generally be estimated only at the national level.

Prevalence of undernourishment is the percentage of the population whose habitual food consumption is insufficient to provide the dietary energy levels that are required to maintain a normal active and healthy life. Data showing as 2.5 may signify a prevalence of undernourishment below 2.5%.
This is the Sustainable Development Goal indicator 2.1.1[https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/metadata/].
Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), uri: http://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#home

Methodology: The prevalence of undernourishment is estimated using a model of the distribution of habitual dietary energy consumption in the population. The indicator is calculated as the probability that an individual's habitual dietary energy consumption falls below the minimum dietary energy requirement (MDER). The model is based on three main parameters: mean dietary energy consumption (DEC), the coefficient of variation (CV) of dietary energy consumption, and the MDER. Food Balance Sheets, nationally representative household surveys, and demographic and anthropometric data are used to estimate these parameters. National estimates are reported as three-year moving averages to account for the low reliability of estimates of some of the underlying parameters.
Statistical concept(s): Undernourishment is the condition in which a person has, on a regular basis, access to an amount of food that is insufficient to provide the dietary energy required for a normal, active and healthy life. Undernourishment differs from malnutrition and undernutrition because it refers to insufficient food intake rather than nutritional status. Although undernourishment is an individual condition, the prevalence of undernourishment is estimated for a population or population group and cannot identify which individuals are undernourished.
